elements.id-string-7: The privacy and security of face data on social media are facing unprecedented challenges as it is vulnerable to unauthorized access and identification.
elements.id-string-8: A common practice for solving this problem is to modify the original data so that it could be protected from being recognized by malicious face recognition (FR) systems.
elements.id-string-9: However, such ``adversarial examples'' obtained by existing methods usually suffer from low transferability and poor image quality, which severely limits the application of these methods in real-world scenarios.
elements.id-string-10: In this paper, we propose a 3D-Aware Adversarial Makeup Generation GAN (3DAM-GAN).
elements.id-string-11: which aims to improve the quality and transferability of synthetic makeup for identity information concealing.
elements.id-string-12: Specifically, a UV-based generator consisting of a novel Makeup Adjustment Module (MAM) and Makeup Transfer Module (MTM) is designed to render realistic and robust makeup with the aid of symmetric characteristics of human faces.
elements.id-string-13: Moreover, a makeup attack mechanism with an ensemble training strategy is proposed to boost the transferability of black-box models.
elements.id-string-14: Extensive experiment results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that 3DAM-GAN could effectively protect faces against various FR models, including both publicly available state-of-the-art models and commercial face verification APIs, such as Face++, Baidu and Aliyun.

elements.id-string-20: \textbf{Low transferability to black-box FR models.}Some methods~\cite{goodfellow2014explaining,brown2017adversarial,madry2017towards} assume that gradients of the target FR model are available when creating adversarial examples.
elements.id-string-21: However, methods built on such ``white-box assumption'' are impractical in real-world scenarios as the FR systems on social media are often inaccessible to users.\textbf{Degraded image quality.}As shown in Fig.~\ref{fig:shouye} (b), although some approaches~\cite{kurakin2017adversarial,dong2018boosting} are able to produce adversarial perturbations with much less intensity than traditional methods, either by injecting noise or attaching patches, they may still fail to preserve the visual quality of original images.
elements.id-string-22: We propose a novel 3D-Aware Adversarial Makeup Generation GAN (3DAM-GAN) to derive adversarial makeup from arbitrary reference images.
elements.id-string-23: It is able to render natural adversarial examples to protect face images from unauthorized FR systems under a more practical black-box attack setting.We design a UV generator consisting of a Makeup Adjustment Module (MAM) and a Makeup Transfer Module (MTM), which help improve the visual fidelity of the synthesized makeup features.
elements.id-string-24: In addition, a UV makeup loss is proposed by leveraging the bilateral symmetry of faces in the UV space to further provide more accurate and robust makeup supervision.We introduce a makeup attack mechanism against various FR models with an ensemble training strategy.
elements.id-string-25: It helps conceal the real identity in makeup generation results from unauthorized FR systems and improve the transferability to black-box setting.Extensive qualitative and quantitative experiments demonstrate that 3DAM-GAN could generate realistic adversarial examples with high success rate of identity protection.
elements.id-string-32: As for (a) makeup generation, we propose a UV generator to transfer the makeup in the UV space while keeping the shape unchanged.
elements.id-string-33: The UV generator contains two novelly designed modules, Makeup Adjustment Module (MAM) and Makeup Transfer Module (MTM), which work together to improve the makeup generation quality.
elements.id-string-34: Moreover, we introduce a novel UV makeup loss $\mathcal{L}_{makeup}^{uv}$ to provide more accurate makeup supervision during training.
elements.id-string-35: As for (b) targeted makeup attack, we consider targeted adversarial attack and perform ensemble training against pre-trained FR models $H=\{H_1,H_2,\cdots,H_K\}$ chosen from various FR systems.}
